claim: Multiple myeloma is an incurable plasma cell malignancy with only a 53% 5-year survival rate.
source: Multiple myeloma is an incurable plasma cell malignancy with only a 53% 5-year survival rate.
evidence: This is a statement of established clinical fact about multiple myeloma prognosis, representing general medical knowledge.

claim: FABP5 was the most highly-expressed FABP isoform in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S and RPMI-8226 cells.
source: We first examined FABP gene expression in MM cell lines and found that FABP5 was the most highly-expressed FABP isoform in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S and RPMI-8226 cells (Supplementary file 1, Fairfield et al., 2021)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from gene expression analysis referenced in Supplementary file 1 and a prior publication (Fairfield et al., 2021).

claim: FABP5 protein was robustly expressed in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S and RPMI-8226 cells.
source: FABP5 protein was also robustly expressed in these cells (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: FABP5 consistently showed expression in haematopoetic/lymphoid lineage lines within the Cancer Cell Line Encyclopedia at the gene level.
source: FABP5 consistently showed the expression in haematopoetic/lymphoid lineage lines within the Cancer Cell Line Encyclopedia (CCLE) at the gene level (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This claim is supported by data from the Cancer Cell Line Encyclopedia database, visualized in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: FABP5 was the most highly expressed FABP at the gene level in MM cell lines specifically.
source: In MM cell lines specifically, FABP5 was the most highly expressed at the gene level (Figure 1B)
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data from MM cell lines shown in Figure 1B.

claim: FABP5 and FABP6 were the most highly expressed FABPs at the protein level in MM cell lines.
source: FABP5 and FABP6 were the most highly expressed at the protein level (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: This claim is supported by proteomic data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Only FABP5 exhibited a negative CERES Score (–0.30) in all 20 MM cell lines in the Broad Institute's Cancer Dependency Map.
source: In the Broad Institute's Cancer Dependency Map (DepMap; Tsherniak et al., 2017), of all the FABPs, only FABP5 exhibited a negative CERES Score (–0.30) in all 20 MM cell lines, demonstrating a strong reliance on FABP5 for their survival (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by CRISPR screening data from the Cancer Dependency Map (Tsherniak et al., 2017), shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: All cancer types within the DepMap database had negative FABP5 CERES values.
source: Interestingly, all cancer types within the DepMap database had negative FABP5 CERES values (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by CRISPR screening data from the Cancer Dependency Map database, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Many fatty acid metabolism genes, including FABP5, had negative CERES scores in MM cells.
source: Importantly, many fatty acid metabolism genes, including FABP5, had negative CERES scores (shown in blue) in MM cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by CRISPR screening data from the Cancer Dependency Map, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: FABP5KO MM.1R cells exhibited a 94% editing efficiency with a ~59% KO efficiency after expansion.
source: FABP5 KO (FABP5KO) MM.1R cells exhibited a 94% editing efficiency with a ~59% KO efficiency after expansion (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by CRISPR-Cas9 editing data and sequencing confirmation shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and B.

claim: An 84% reduction in FABP5 expression was observed in the edited pool of MM.1R cells.
source: We observed an 84% reduction in FABP5 expression in the edited pool (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C), confirming functional FABP5 knockdown.
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C.

claim: FABP4 expression was not altered in FABP5 KO MM.1R cells.
source: FABP4 expression was not altered (Figure 1—figure supplement 3D)
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3D.

claim: FABP6 expression was increased in the FABP5-edited MM.1R cells.
source: but FABP6 expression was increased in the edited cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3E.

claim: FABP5 KO cells showed a slight reduction in cell numbers at 48, 72, and 96 hr, versus controls.
source: FABP5 KO cells showed a slight reduction in cell numbers at 48, 72, and 96 hr, versus controls (Figure 1—figure supplement 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RealTime-Glo cell viability assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3F.

claim: BMS309403 has Ki values in solution of <2, 250, and 350 nM for FABP4, FABP3, and FABP5, respectively.
source: Ligand-binding assays determined that BMS309403 has Ki values in solution of <2, 250, and 350 nM for FABP4, FABP3, and FABP5, and that SBFI-26 has Ki values of 900 and 400 nM for FABP5 and FABP7, respectively, as reported on the manufacturers' datasheets (Hsu et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by ligand-binding assay data reported by the manufacturer and cited from Hsu et al., 2017.

claim: SBFI-26 has Ki values of 900 and 400 nM for FABP5 and FABP7, respectively.
source: Ligand-binding assays determined that BMS309403 has Ki values in solution of <2, 250, and 350 nM for FABP4, FABP3, and FABP5, and that SBFI-26 has Ki values of 900 and 400 nM for FABP5 and FABP7, respectively, as reported on the manufacturers' datasheets (Hsu et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by ligand-binding assay data reported by the manufacturer and cited from Hsu et al., 2017.

claim: BMS309403 and SBFI-26 consistently demonstrated dose-dependent decreases in myeloma cell numbers in all 7 MM lines screened at 72 hr.
source: BMS309403 and SBFI-26 consistently demonstrated dose-dependent decreases in myeloma cell numbers, in all 7 MM lines screened, at 72 hr (Figure 1C and D; Supplementary files 2 and 3)
evidence: This claim is supported by dose-response curve data shown in Figure 1C and D and Supplementary files 2 and 3.

claim: BMS309403 (50 µM), SBFI-26 (50 µM), or the combination (50 µM BMS309403 +50 µM SBFI-26) reduced cell numbers at 24, 48, and 72 hr by 39%, 42%, and 83%, respectively in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S cells.
source: BMS309403 (50 µM), SBFI-26 (50 µM), or the combination (50 µM BMS309403 +50 µM SBFI-26) reduced cell numbers at 24, 48, and 72 hr by 39%, 42%, and 83%, respectively in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S cells (Figure 1E)
evidence: This claim is supported by cell viability assay data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Non-cancerous cells were much less sensitive to FABPi than myeloma cells.
source: Non-cancerous cells were much less sensitive to FABPi (Figure 1F)
evidence: This claim is supported by CellTiter-Glo analysis of human mesenchymal stem cells shown in Figure 1F.

claim: No change in amount or localization of FABP5 protein after treatment with FABPi was observed by immunofluorescence at 24 hr in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S or RPMI-8226 cells.
source: No change in amount or localization of FABP5 protein after treatment with FABPi was observed by immunofluorescence (Figure 1—figure supplements 5 and 6) at 24 hr in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S or RPMI-8226 cells
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 5 and 6.

claim: No change in FABP5 protein was observed by western blotting at 24, 48, or 72 hr in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S cells after FABPi treatment.
source: or by western blotting at 24, 48, or 72 hr in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 7A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 7A and B.

claim: Gene expression of FABP3, FABP4, FABP5, and FABP6 were not consistently altered with FABPi treatments.
source: Gene expression of FABP3, FABP4, FABP5, and FABP6 were also not consistently altered with treatments (Figure 1—figure supplement 7C) as assessed by qRT-PCR.
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 7C.

claim: Recombinant FABP4 and FABP5 did not affect MM.1S cell number.
source: Recombinant FABP4 and FABP5 did not affect MM.1S cell number (Figure 1—figure supplement 8A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase activity analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 8A and B.

claim: Principal component analysis demonstrated that the FABP inhibitor groups exhibited distinct gene expression profiles.
source: Principal component analysis (PCA) demonstrated that the FABP inhibitor groups exhibited distinct gene expression profiles, and that the combination treatment differed the most from vehicle-treated cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by PCA analysis of RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Over 14,000 genes were analyzed in RNA-Seq, revealing 93 significant differentially expressed genes within all three treatment groups, compared to the vehicle control (FDR <0.2): 90 downregulated and 3 upregulated.
source: Over 14,000 genes were analyzed, revealing 93 significant differentially expressed (DE) genes within all three treatment groups, compared to the vehicle control (FDR <0.2): 90 downregulated and 3 upregulated (Figure 2B; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression analysis shown in Figure 2B and Supplementary file 4.

claim: Significantly lower levels of 5-hydroxymethylcytosine were observed in cells treated with FABPi compared to vehicle-treated cells.
source: Consistent with decreased levels of transcription, we also observed significantly lower levels of 5-hydroxymethylcytosine in cells treated with FABPi compared to vehicle-treated cells (Figure 2C), suggesting decreases in active chromatin.
evidence: This claim is supported by global hydroxymethylation DNA analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: FABP depletion is linked to DNA methylation signatures in other cancers.
source: This finding is consistent with previous reports linking FABP depletion to DNA methylation signatures in other cancers (Mukherjee et al., 2020; Yan et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Mukherjee et al., 2020; Yan et al., 2018).

claim: 15 IPA canonical pathways were commonly dysregulated in all three FABPi treatment groups including Cell Cycle: G2/M DNA Damage Checkpoint Regulation, EIF2 Signaling, Sirtuin Signaling Pathway, and the NER pathway.
source: In total, 15 IPA canonical pathways were commonly dysregulated in all three treatment groups including Cell Cycle: G2/M DNA Damage Checkpoint Regulation, EIF2 Signaling, Sirtuin Signaling Pathway, and the NER pathway (Figure 2D; Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by Ingenuity Pathway Analysis of RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 2D and Supplementary file 5.

claim: The one upregulated pathway according to STRING was 'cellular response to interferon gamma signaling' in the combination group.
source: The one upregulated pathway according to STRING was 'cellular response to interferon gamma signaling' in the combination group (Figure 2E; Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by STRING database pathway analysis shown in Figure 2E and Supplementary file 6.

claim: Both IPA and STRING databases revealed commonly downregulated pathways related to the unfolded protein response (UPR) or ER stress responses for BMS309403, SBFI-26, and the combination.
source: Interestingly, both IPA and STRING databases revealed commonly downregulated pathways related to the unfolded protein response (UPR) or ER stress responses for BMS309403 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C), SBFI-26 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3, and the combination Figure 2D and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by pathway analysis from IPA and STRING databases shown in multiple figures.

claim: Three of the five downregulated Reactome pathways in the combination group were related to UPR or ER stress.
source: Three of the five downregulated Reactome pathways in the combination group were related to UPR or ER stress (Figure 2F)
evidence: This claim is supported by Reactome pathway analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Downregulation of total XBP1 by the combination treatment was confirmed after 24 hr.
source: Downregulation of total XBP1 by the combination treatment was confirmed after 24 hr (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B)
evidence: This claim is supported by semi-quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3B.

claim: MYC was a central node in STRING analysis.
source: Interestingly, MYC, a known oncogene, was a central node in STRING analysis (Figure 2F)
evidence: This claim is supported by STRING network analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: MYC was among the top 10 most downregulated genes in RNA-Seq from combination treatments.
source: and among the top 10 most downregulated genes in RNA-Seq from combination treatments (Supplementary file 8).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq differential expression data in Supplementary file 8.

claim: PCA analysis of proteomic data showed a tight grouping of samples based on treatments.
source: PCA analysis showed a tight grouping of samples based on treatments (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This claim is supported by PCA analysis of proteomic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: 15 proteins were commonly upregulated and 15 were commonly downregulated between all FABPi treatments in proteomic analysis.
source: 15 proteins were commonly upregulated and 15 were commonly downregulated between all treatments (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, C; Supplementary files 16 and 17).
evidence: This claim is supported by proteomic analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, C and Supplementary files 16 and 17.

claim: CCL3 was upregulated by SBFI-26, BMS309403, and their combination in proteomics, and upregulated by the combination treatments in RNA-Seq.
source: CCL3, a chemokine for monocytes, macrophages, and neutrophils, was upregulated by SBFI-26, BMS309403, and their combination in proteomics, and upregulated by the combination treatments in RNA-Seq.
evidence: This claim is supported by both proteomic and RNA-Seq data comparing the two datasets.

claim: Ki67 and PTMA were both significantly downregulated in the combination treatment in RNA-Seq and proteomics, and in the single drug treatments in proteomics.
source: Ki67, a proliferation marker, and PTMA, a negative regulator of apoptosis, were both significantly downregulated in the combination treatment in RNA-Seq and proteomics, and in the single drug treatments in proteomics (Figure 3B)
evidence: This claim is supported by both proteomic and RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: EIF2 Signaling had the highest negative Z-score for all FABPi treatments in proteomics according to IPA analysis.
source: IPA analysis revealed 'EIF2 Signaling' to have the highest negative Z-score for all FABPi treatments in proteomics (Figure 3E; Figure 3—figure supplement 4A, Figure 3—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by IPA pathway analysis of proteomic data shown in Figure 3E and supplementary figures.

claim: IPA 'Cell Death and Survival' heatmap analysis showed increases in cell death and apoptosis pathways and decreases in cell viability pathways after FABPi combination treatment.
source: IPA 'Cell Death and Survival' heatmap analysis showed increases in cell death and apoptosis pathways and decreases in cell viability pathways after FABPi combination treatment (Figure 3F; Figure 3—figure supplements 4B and 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by IPA pathway analysis of proteomic data shown in Figure 3F and supplementary figures.

claim: MYC was the most significant predicted upstream regulator, found to be strongly inhibited in the BMS309403, SBFI-26, and combination treatments from IPA proteomic analysis.
source: Interestingly, MYC was the most significant predicted upstream regulator, found to be strongly inhibited in the BMS309403, SBFI-26, and combination treatments from IPA proteomic analysis (Supplementary files 18-20).
evidence: This claim is supported by IPA upstream regulator analysis of proteomic data in Supplementary files 18-20.

claim: Decreased MYC expression was confirmed in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S cells treated with the FABPi combination.
source: We confirmed decreased MYC expression in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S cells treated with the FABPi combination, and also saw a trend for this in 5TGM1-TK cells treated with SBFI-26 (Figure 3—figure supplement 6A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6A and B.

claim: MYC protein level was decreased in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S cells at 24, 48, and 72 hr with FABPi.
source: MYC protein level was also decreased in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S cells at 24, 48, and 72 hr with FABPi (Figure 4A and B)
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: Treatment with BMS309403 induced aberrant gene expression of 171 genes known to be regulated by MYC in RNA-Seq data, with 138 of those having expression patterns consistent with MYC inhibition.
source: In RNA-Seq data, treatment with BMS309403 induced aberrant gene expression of 171 genes known to be regulated by MYC (Supplementary file 21), with 138 of those having expression patterns consistent with MYC inhibition.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis in Supplementary file 21.

claim: Co-treatment with FABPi induced changes in 91 genes modulated by MYC, with 68 consistent with MYC downregulation.
source: Similarly, co-treatment induced changes in 91 genes modulated by MYC (Figure 3—figure supplement 7; 68 consistent with MYC downregulation)
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 7.

claim: 29 MYC targets were aberrantly expressed with SBFI-26 treatment, with 18 consistent with MYC downregulation.
source: while 29 MYC targets were aberrantly expressed with SBFI-26 treatment (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D; 18 consistent with MYC downregulation).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D.

claim: MYC inhibition alone dramatically reduced cell numbers at 72 hr.
source: MYC inhibition alone dramatically reduced cell numbers at 72 hr, as expected
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from MYC inhibitor treatment experiments.

claim: FABP inhibition had less of an effect on MM cells when MYC was already inhibited.
source: and FABP inhibition had less of an effect on MM cells when MYC was already inhibited (seen by a slope of ~0 for the black lines) (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by dose-response curve data with combined MYC and FABP inhibition shown in Figure 4E and F.

claim: All FABPi treatments decreased basal mitochondrial oxygen consumption rates and OCR dedicated to ATP production after 24 hr treatments.
source: After 24 hr treatments, all FABPi treatments decreased basal mitochondrial oxygen consumption rates (OCR) and OCR dedicated to ATP production (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by Seahorse Cell Mito Stress Test data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Maximal respiration and spare respiratory capacity were decreased with SBFI-26 and combination treatments.
source: Maximal respiration and spare respiratory capacity were decreased with SBFI-26 and combination treatments, suggesting FABP inhibition reduces the ability of MM cells to meet their energetic demands.
evidence: This claim is supported by Seahorse Cell Mito Stress Test data and represents an inference from the observed metabolic changes.

claim: Etomoxir treatment caused a slight, but significant reduction in OCR when it was administered, demonstrating some reliance of MM cells on FAO for mitochondrial respiration.
source: Interestingly, etoxomir treatment caused a slight, but significant reduction in OCR when it was administered, demonstrating some reliance of MM cells on FAO for mitochondrial respiration.
evidence: This claim is supported by Seahorse metabolic assay data with etomoxir treatment.

claim: FABPi had a much greater effect on MM mitochondrial respiration than etomoxir alone.
source: However, the FABPi had a much greater effect on MM mitochondrial respiration than etoxomir alone, suggesting that FABPi treatment inhibited mitochondrial respiration through another mechanism.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of Seahorse metabolic assay data between FABPi and etomoxir treatments, with inference about mechanism.

claim: GFP+/Luc+MM.1S cells treated with BMS309403 or the combination (BMS309403 +SBFI-26) had decreased TMRE staining.
source: GFP+/Luc+MM.1S cells treated with BMS309403 or the combination (BMS309403 +SBFI-26) had decreased TMRE staining (Figure 5—figure supplement 3), suggesting that BMS309403 damages MM cell mitochondria.
evidence: This claim is supported by TMRE mitochondrial membrane potential assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3, with inference about mitochondrial damage.

claim: The combination FABPi treatment significantly increased total ROS at 24, 48, or 72 hr in MM.1S (ATCC), U266 and OPM2 cells.
source: CellROX staining showed that the combination FABPi treatment significantly increased total ROS at 24, 48, or 72 hr in MM.1S (ATCC), U266 and OPM2 cells (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplements 4A and 5A, 6 A).
evidence: This claim is supported by CellROX flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5A and supplementary figures.

claim: In MM.1S (ATCC), BMS309403 and the FABPi combination increased superoxides over 72 hr.
source: We also found changes in superoxide, a ROS subspecies measured by MitoSOX, after FABP inhibition; in MM.1S (ATCC), BMS309403 and the FABPi combination increased superoxides over 72 hr (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by MitoSOX flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 4B.

claim: In U266, the FABPi combination increased superoxides at each time point, and BMS309403 increased superoxides at 48 and 72 hr.
source: In U266, the FABPi combination increased superoxides at each time point, and BMS309403 increased superoxides at 48 and 72 hr (Figure 5—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by MitoSOX flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5B.

claim: In OPM2, all FABPi treatments increased superoxides at all timepoints.
source: In OPM2, all FABPi treaments increased superoxides at all timepoints (Figure 5—figure supplement 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by MitoSOX flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 6B.

claim: FABPi combination treatment increased the G0/G1 population at 24, 48, and 72 hr in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S cells.
source: In GFP+/Luc +MM.1 S, FABPi combination treatment increased the G0/G1 population at 24, 48, and 72 hr, and decreased G2/M at 48 and 72 hr, suggesting a G0/G1 arrest and a negative impact on cell cycle progression (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell cycle analysis data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 7.

claim: FABPi combination treatment decreased G2/M at 48 and 72 hr in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S cells.
source: In GFP+/Luc +MM.1 S, FABPi combination treatment increased the G0/G1 population at 24, 48, and 72 hr, and decreased G2/M at 48 and 72 hr, suggesting a G0/G1 arrest and a negative impact on cell cycle progression (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell cycle analysis data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 7.

claim: FABPi combination treatment increased apoptosis in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S cells at all three time points (24, 48, 72 hr).
source: FABPi combination treatment also increased apoptosis in GFP+/Luc +MM.1 S cells at all three time points, and SBFI-26 did as well at 72 hr (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: SBFI-26 increased apoptosis in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S cells at 72 hr.
source: FABPi combination treatment also increased apoptosis in GFP+/Luc +MM.1 S cells at all three time points, and SBFI-26 did as well at 72 hr (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by apoptosis assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: In GFP+/Luc+MM.1S, 100 µM of BMS309403 induced larger impacts on apoptosis, cell cycle arrest, and Ki67 expression than all other treatments.
source: Interestingly, in GFP+/Luc +MM.1 S, 100 µM of BMS309403 induced larger impacts on apoptosis, cell cycle arrest, and Ki67 expression than all other treatments (Figure 5—figure supplement 8) suggesting it may be more effective than SBFI-26 in this cell line.
evidence: This claim is supported by dose-response data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 8, with inference about relative efficacy.

claim: In RPMI-8226 cells, 100 µM of single inhibitors elicited similar responses to combination treatment inhibitors (50 µM BMS309403 +50 µM SBFI-26).
source: In RPMI-8226 cells, apoptosis and cell cycle arrest were also induced with the combination or single inhibitors (Figure 5—figure supplement 9). Interestingly, in this cell line, 100 µM of single inhibitors elicited similar responses to combination treatment inhibitors (50 µM BMS309403 +50 µM SBFI-26), suggesting that FABP inhibitors may have slightly different efficacies in different MM cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by dose-response data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 9, with inference about cell line-specific efficacy.

claim: Dexamethasone and FABPi showed promising, additive effects on cell numbers and apoptosis in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S, OPM2, and RPMI-8226 cells.
source: We subsequently investigated the combination of FABPi with dexamethasone, a first-line therapy for MM patients. Dexamethasone and FABPi showed promising, additive effects on cell numbers and apoptosis in GFP+/Luc+MM.1S, OPM2, and RPMI-8226 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 10)
evidence: This claim is supported by combination treatment data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 10.

claim: Bone mineral density (BMD), but not bone mineral content (BMC), was slightly lower after BMS309403 treatment in the first SCID-beige xenograft model.
source: Bone mineral density (BMD), but not bone mineral content (BMC), was slightly lower after BMS309403 treatment (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, C), although this group also started with a slightly lower BMD
evidence: This claim is supported by DEXA analysis data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: Fat mass, but not lean mass was decreased with the combination treatment in the first SCID-beige xenograft model.
source: and fat mass, but not lean mass was decreased with the combination treatment (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: This claim is supported by DEXA analysis data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: FABPi did not influence mouse weight in the first SCID-beige xenograft model.
source: FABPi did not influence mouse weight (Figure 6A)
evidence: This claim is supported by mouse weight data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: A difference in tumor burden assessed by BLI was detected at day 21 with all FABPi versus vehicle in the first SCID-beige xenograft model, and this difference continued throughout the study.
source: but a difference in tumor burden assessed by BLI was detected at day 21 with all FABPi versus vehicle, and this difference continued throughout the study (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by bioluminescence imaging data shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: Mice receiving FABPi survived longer than the vehicle-treated mice in the first SCID-beige xenograft model.
source: Consistent with reduced tumor burden, mice receiving FABPi survived longer than the vehicle-treated mice (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Mice treated with 5 mg/kg BMS309403 showed increased survival in the GFP+/Luc+ 5TGM1-TK/KaLwRij syngeneic model.
source: Similarly, in the GFP+/Luc+ 5TGM1-TK/KaLwRij syngeneic model (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A), mice treated with 5 mg/kg BMS309403 showed increased survival (Figure 6E)
evidence: This claim is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: BMS309403 treatment did not cause significant body weight changes in the GFP+/Luc+ 5TGM1-TK/KaLwRij syngeneic model.
source: without significant body weight changes (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by mouse weight data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2B.

claim: In the second cohort of SCID-Beige mice, treatments had only slight, non-significant effects on tumor burden.
source: However, in this cohort, treatments had on slight, non-significant effects on tumor burden (Figure 7B and C)
evidence: This claim is supported by bioluminescence imaging data shown in Figure 7B and C.

claim: In the second cohort of SCID-Beige mice, FABPi had no effect on survival.
source: and no effect on survivial (Figure 7D).
evidence: This claim is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis shown in Figure 7D.

claim: ~70% of myeloma patient cases exhibited moderate-to-high expression of FABP5 (defined as >10 counts) in the CoMMpass database.
source: In the CoMMpass database, ~70% of myeloma patient cases exhibited moderate-to-high expression of FABP5 (defined as >10 counts; Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of the CoMMpass patient database shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Patients with higher MM cell FABP5 expression had significantly shorter overall survival than those with lower expression in the Zhan dataset.
source: The Zhan dataset indicated that patients with higher MM cell FABP5 expression had significantly shorter overall survival (OS) than those with lower expression (Zhan et al., 2006), (Figure 8A and B)
evidence: This claim is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis of the Zhan et al., 2006 dataset shown in Figure 8A and B.

claim: The association between high FABP5 expression and shorter overall survival was confirmed in the Mulligan dataset.
source: which was confirmed in the Mulligan dataset (Mulligan et al., 2007, Figure 8C).
evidence: This claim is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis of the Mulligan et al., 2007 dataset shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The Carrasco dataset showed a shorter progression-free survival (PFS) in MM patients with high versus low FABP5 expression.
source: Similarly, the Carrasco dataset showed a shorter progression-free survival (PFS) in MM patients with high versus low FABP5 expression (Figure 8D, Carrasco et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis of the Carrasco et al., 2006 dataset shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Patients of the high-risk/poor prognosis subtype had higher FABP5 expression than those in the more favorable subtypes in the Zhan dataset.
source: Moreover, patients of the high-risk/poor prognosis subtype had higher FABP5 expression than those in the more favorable subtypes (Zhan et al., 2006, Figure 8E).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of FABP5 expression across MM molecular subtypes in the Zhan et al., 2006 dataset shown in Figure 8E.

claim: Relapsed patients showed increased FABP5 expression versus newly-diagnosed patients in the Chng dataset.
source: In the Chng dataset (Chng et al., 2007), relapsed patients showed increased FABP5 expression versus newly-diagnosed patients (Figure 8F).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of FABP5 expression in newly-diagnosed versus relapsed patients in the Chng et al., 2007 dataset shown in Figure 8F.

claim: Worse PFS and OS in patients with elevated FABP5 expression levels was confirmed in the CoMMpass dataset (log-rank-value for high vs. low expression,<0.0001 for both PFS and OS).
source: Worse PFS and OS in patients with elevated FABP5 expression levels was then confirmed in the CoMMpass dataset (log-rank-value for high vs. low expression,<0.0001 for both PFS and OS; Figure 8—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This claim is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis of the CoMMpass dataset shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1B and C.
